name: Europe hybrid attacks
summary: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 17 European flights on 5 Nov, the third wave in a week; no state blamed
state: False bomb threats affected at least 17 flights across Europe on 5 Nov after similar hoaxes earlier in the week; no explosives were found (ABC News Australia). Bulgaria reported three emergency landings and Czech police rated threats to Prague-bound flights as low credibility (The National). Remote attacks on supermarket refrigeration hit EU stores on 2 Nov. No state has been formally blamed.
for_you: Expect occasional diversions and delays on European flights; follow airline and airport advice.
rubric_hit: Repeated aviation disruption; no airport shutdowns or state attribution yet

sources.title: ABC News — Bomb threat hoaxes divert planes over Europe for third time this week
The National — European flights diverted after second wave of bomb threats

why: Sabotage, arson and drone incursions over airports and bases are how state confrontation reaches daily life in the UK and Europe.
drivers: Russia–NATO tensions, drone and cyber capabilities, proxy recruitment, elections.

rubric.alert: Repeated airport or infrastructure shutdowns across several countries, or sabotage causing casualties or a major outage.
rubric.watch: Drone incursions close an airport or military base, or a sabotage incident is attributed to a state.
rubric.normal: No significant attributed sabotage or airspace incursions in Europe this week.
